performers: Orquestra de música antiga de l’Esmuc; Alba Roca, concertmaster and director
intro: Purcell’s chaconne from The Fairy Queen keeps its three-beat dance going while the bass disappears for sixteen bars. Alba Roca directs the ESMUC early-music orchestra in a piece that can feel wonderfully light on its feet.

sections.label: A · Dotted strings over a walking bass
sections.mNote: Long-short violin phrases above three steady bass notes

sections.label: B · The violins begin to run
sections.mNote: Quicker violin notes keep the same three-beat dance

sections.label: C · Three strings, no bass
sections.mNote: Violins and viola trade short phrases

sections.label: D · The bass steps back in
sections.mNote: Short bass notes alternate with rests

sections.label: E · The bass runs beneath the violins
sections.mNote: Moving bass notes support the final dance phrases

cues.title: Three steps in the bass
cues.text: The bass takes three even steps in each bar. Above it, the violins and viola lean on dotted rhythms — a long note followed by a short one. The tune keeps lifting off that steady tread.
cues.evidence: Purcell, Suite from The Fairy Queen, edited by J. S. Shedlock, typeset by Bart Dunn, Chaconne, bars 1–16, printed p. 48. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/69/IMSLP435506-PMLP237007-Suite_from_The_Fairy_Queen_Complete.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A dance in the museum
cues.text: This performance takes place among the keyboards of Barcelona’s Museu de la Música. Alba Roca directs the ESMUC early-music orchestra on 7 April 2018; student sound engineer Marc Urrutia records the concert.
cues.evidence: The ESMUC recording credits name the Sala de teclats, Museu de la Música de Barcelona, Alba Roca, Marc Urrutia and the concert date. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Purcell_TheFairyQueen_ActV_Chaconne_Z629_Esmuc.flac

cues.title: The bass sits out
cues.text: For sixteen bars, the bass has nothing to play. The violins and viola pass little phrases between them, often leaving the first beat empty in the violins. The three-beat dance continues on these lighter feet.
cues.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 49–64, printed pp. 50–51: the basso rests throughout; violin rests and viola entries alternate.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Running towards the close
cues.text: The bass begins moving more freely beneath the violins, with quick notes joining the dance. The first violin answers with little flourishes. All four parts have work to do again.
cues.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, printed pp. 51–53, especially the running basso from bar 82.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: The violins quicken
transitions.from: A · Dotted strings over a walking bass
transitions.to: B · The violins begin to run
transitions.how: The opening phrases settle, and both violins take up quicker dotted figures. The basso keeps its three crotchets to the bar; the viola punctuates the new violin writing with notes and rests. The dance stays in 3/4.
transitions.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 16–22, printed p. 48: quicker violin figures above the continuing bass crotchets.

transitions.title: The bass leaves the dance
transitions.from: B · The violins begin to run
transitions.how: After the four parts arrive together at the end of the phrase, the basso rests for sixteen bars. The viola starts the next figure while the violins leave a rest on the first beat, then answer. The upper strings now have the dance to themselves.
transitions.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 48–64, printed pp. 50–51: the basso stops at bar 49; the three upper parts continue.

transitions.title: The bass returns between rests
transitions.to: D · The bass steps back in
transitions.how: The basso returns with three repeated crotchets. Then bass and viola alternate short notes with rests beneath the violins’ dotted phrases. The returning low line has room to breathe between its steps.
transitions.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 65–77, printed p. 51: repeated bass notes at bar 65, followed by notes separated by rests.

transitions.title: Quick notes reach the bass
transitions.from: D · The bass steps back in
transitions.to: E · The bass runs beneath the violins
transitions.how: The first violin adds quick flourishes to its dotted phrases. Beneath it, the basso moves from longer notes into running figures of its own. Those low notes fill the spaces left by the earlier rests and carry the dance towards its close.
transitions.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 78–84 and following, printed pp. 51–53: violin flourishes and the running basso from bar 82.

source.title: Purcell, The Fairy Queen — instrumental suite, Bart Dunn typesetting after Shedlock
source.locator: Chaconne, printed pp. 48–53: two violin parts, viola and basso. The cello desk represents the written basso part.

timeline.note: The violins and viola play dotted phrases above three steady bass notes in each bar.
The basso rests for bars 49–64; the violins and viola pass short phrases between them.
The basso returns with repeated notes, then leaves rests between its phrases.
Running bass notes support the violins’ dotted phrases and little flourishes.

fields.label: Work version
fields.value: Original four-part instrumental dance; sounding pitch approximately A=415
fields.note: The file identifies the Act V Chaconne. Approximate pitch is inferred by comparing its written C-major ending with the recording’s prominent sustained peaks near 494–495 Hz, about a semitone below modern C5. The session source does not state a tuning reference; no exact temperament or edition is claimed.
